title: Flank Pain & Urinary Infection Variant 31

patient.name: Charles Lopez
patient.chief_complaint: Left flank pain and high fever
patient.initial_statement: I have this severe throbbing pain in my lower left back. It extends to my side. I've also had high fevers, shaking chills, and it hurts when I pee.

symptoms: Sharp throbbing pain in the left back (flank / costovertebral angle)
Documented high fever and systemic chills
Dysuria (burning painful urination) and urinating frequently
Stomach nausea and vomiting twice this morning
Symptoms started as mild bladder pressure 3 days ago
past_medical_history: Frequent UTIs, none previously requiring hospitalization
allergies: No known drug or food allergies
family_history: Mother has history of kidney stones
social_history: Non-smoker, high school teacher, drinks about 1L of water daily
review_of_systems: Cardiovascular: pulse rate is 105 bpm, no active chest pain except as noted.

patient_beliefs: I hope this is just a temporary strain that will pass.
I've been under a lot of stress with my job.
I'm terrified this might be something permanent or fatal.
patient_goals: Determine the core cause of these symptoms.
Verify whether there is emergency intervention required.
Get diagnostic results explained to me step by step.

examinations.name: General Physical Examination
examinations.result: Alert, looks moderately ill, shivering due to fever. In moderate distress.

examinations.name: Abdominal Examination
examinations.result: Abdomen is soft, completely non-tender on superficial and deep palpation. Epigastrium non-tender.

investigations.name: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG)
investigations.result: Normal sinus rhythm, regular rate 72 bpm, no ST/T abnormalities.

investigations.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
investigations.result: WBC: 15.2 x10^9/L (Elevated), Hb: 12.8 g/dL, Platelets: 280 x10^9/L.
investigations.interpretation: Marked leukocytosis confirming active systemic bacterial infection.

investigations.name: Serum Electrolytes Panel
investigations.interpretation: Serum electrolytes are within normal range.

investigations.name: Chest X-ray (CXR)
investigations.result: Both lungs are hypolucent, no vascular congestion or consolidation.

investigations.name: CT Angiography of Chest
investigations.result: Normal caliber aorta, no luminal narrowing, no dissection flap visible.

investigations.name: CT Scan of Head (cranial assessment)
investigations.result: No acute hemorrhage, infarct, or midline shifts found in cranial structures.
investigations.interpretation: Normal CT Scan of the Head.

investigations.name: CT Scan of Abdomen & Pelvis
investigations.result: Stomach, liver, bowel loops, and appendix are normal size with no inflammatory changes.
investigations.interpretation: Normal CT Scan of the Abdomen.

investigations.name: Urinalysis and Urine Culture
investigations.result: Turbid color, pH 6.5, Positive Nitrites, Positive Leukocyte Esterase, WBC: >50 per high-power-field (hpf), Urine Bacteria: Moderate.
investigations.interpretation: Active bacterial urinary tract infection (UTI) involving pyuria and bacteriuria; matches Pyelonephritis.

investigations.name: Duplex Vascular Leg Ultrasound
investigations.result: Normal patency of left and right femoral veins with complete color Doppler signal.

expected_pathway.label: Meet Charles Lopez (Left flank pain and high fever)
Interview Urinary Symptoms, Chills & Flank Pain
Perform Costovertebral Angle (CVA) Tenderness & Abdominal Exam
Order Urinalysis and Urine Culture (Identify Pyuria & Nitrites)
Order Complete Blood Count (CBC) (Assess Systemic Infection)
Diagnose Acute Pyelonephritis & Initiate Targeted Antibiotics
